<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/">What Novis claims</a><span class="nv-section-count">5</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Who the language is for, the three things it promises, and the ordering that decides every trade below.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#audience">Novis is built for web applications of every kind, with command-line tooling second</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#three-claims">Novis claims three things, and &quot;faster than PHP&quot; is not one of them</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#no-compatibility-promise">The PHP-shaped syntax is an on-ramp, and no document may promise compatibility</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#slice-ranking">When two slices compete, the one that gets a working application sooner wins</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/claims-and-priorities/#memory-priority">Memory buys security, correctness, latency and simplicity — bounded, attributable and stated</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>

<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/">Names, files and programs</a><span class="nv-section-count">11</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">How a name reaches the file that declares it — while compiling, with no loader running anywhere.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#implementing"><code>Core\Program::implementing&lt;T&gt;()</code> lists every concrete class that is a <code>T</code>, for an interface or a class, and it expands while compiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#implementing-with"><code>Core\Program::implementingWith&lt;I, T&gt;($member)</code> joins the enumeration with one attribute per class, and it expands while compiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#constructors"><code>Core\Program::constructors&lt;T, C&gt;()</code> lists the enumeration's classes with one closure each, typed by <code>C</code>, and it expands while compiling</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#compile-target">A compile target changes the host context, never the language</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#no-runtime-autoload">A name reaches its file while compiling; there is no runtime loader of any kind</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#autoload"><code>autoload</code> maps a prefix to roots, resolved relative to the file that declares it</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#one-declaration-per-autoloaded-file">A file reached by autoload declares exactly one thing, under the name the map finds it by</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#path-case">A <code>require</code> path is compared against the on-disk entry exactly, on every OS</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#path-literals-resolve-from-their-file">A relative path literal at a path parameter names a file beside the source file that wrote it, and a relative path built at run time throws</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#program-id"><code>Core\Program::id()</code> is 64 hex characters naming this program's code and environment</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/names-and-files/#bundle-trust-domain">A bundled executable is one trust domain: a program, never a service</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li></ol>
</section>
<section class="nv-section">
<h2 class="nv-section-title"><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/">The first-party framework</a><span class="nv-section-count">6</span></h2>
<p class="nv-section-blurb">Novis ships the framework, split into a privileged half in the binary and an opinionated half as a package.</p>
<ol class="nv-rule-list"><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#first-party-framework">Novis ships the framework, split by the standard-library placement tests</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#framework-core-half">The privileged half of the framework is <code>Core</code>, compiled into the binary</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="shipped">Shipped</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#framework-web-package">The opinionated half is <code>nvs/web</code>, a first-party package providing the <code>Web</code> namespace</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#framework-refusals">The framework has no ORM, no runtime container, and no second way to do anything</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span><span class="nv-rule-list-flag" title="Differs from PHP">PHP</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#no-migration-runner">No migration runner ships until migration semantics are decided</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li><li><a href="/docs/rules/programs/the-framework/#nvs-new"><code>nvs new</code> writes an application that runs before it is edited</a><span class="nv-rule-list-status" data-status="designed">Designed</span></li></ol>
</section>
